newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds slip on higher than forecast CPI.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds slip on higher than forecast CPI.

text.p: Higher than expected Danish May consumer price data sent bond prices down slightly on Friday leaving Danish-German yield spreads wider than foreseen.
The market's further movment was seen as depending on developments in U.S. treasuries.
At 1215 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down to 111.73, yielding 6.21 percent, from Thursday's 112.10 and 6.15 percent yield.Turnover was 2.0 billion crowns.
The seven percent 2007 fell to 104.30, yielding 6.41 percent, from Thursday's 104.50. Turnover was 700 million crowns.
The 2006's yield gap with Germany widened to 46 basis points from Thursday's 42 bp, while the the 2007-bund differential grew to 65 basis points from 64.
The 2006's September future fell 0.44 point to 110.94 with 121 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.80 point to 89.95.
The crown firmed slightly, to 3.8079 per mark from 3.8080 --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
